subject: warnings when using sam() with categorical indicators

messages.author: 7bd5f89131fa4be5
messages.subject: warnings when using sam() with categorical indicators
parts:
Dear all, 

I plan to run a local SAM model using the sam() function in lavaan. I tried this out using Example 1 of the Rosseel & Loh (2022) paper (the dataset and script can be found here). This works fine, but for my own research, I will have categorical indicators (mostly Likert items, some dichotomous items). I recently saw here that sam() now also works with categorical indicators, which is great.  

I tried whether this works by declaring the indicator variables of the example dataset as ordered factors, and running the following model: 

model <- '
  # measurement part
    ost   =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
    self  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
    other =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  # structural part
    ost   ~ b1*self + b2*other + c*sol + age + gender
    self  ~ a1*sol + age + gender
    other ~ a2*sol + age + gender
  # residual correlations
    self ~~ other '

fit.lsam_o2 <- sam(model, data = Data2, sam.method = "local", ordered = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "y1", "y2", "y3", "y4"))

When I run this model, I get the following warnings: 

Warning messages:
1: In sam(model, data = Data2, sam.method = "local", ordered = c("x1",  :
  lavaan WARNING: sam() does not support conditional.x = TRUE (yet)
  -> switching to conditional.x = FALSE
2: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

I am struggling to understand what these warnings mean, and what the implications are for my analyses (i.e., is this a problem?). If anyone could help me out, that would be extremely helpful. 

Re Warning 1: Here I read a more technical explanation about what conditional.x = FALSE means. I have to admit I have not been able to wrap my head around whether this would be problematic, or not. Are there situations were this would be problematic? 
I also read this here: "By default, in the categorical case we use conditional.x = TRUE. Therefore, any cases with missing values on the exogenous covariates will be deleted listwise from the data first." I can see how that would be problematic in case of missing values. I do have missing values, but I plan to use multiple imputation to create multiple complete datasets, so I think this should not be an issue.  

Re Warning 2: Here is a post that concerns that same warning, and which seems to state that if you want to use WLSMV as estimator (which I do), conditional.x needs  to be TRUE, otherwise something goes wrong in the estimation stage. However, this seems to contradict Yves Rosseel's (more recent) statement that sam() now also works for categorical variables. Does anyone know more about this, or about Warning 2 in general? 

Thanks very much! 

Best, 
Floor

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: warnings when using sam() with categorical indicators
parts:
Warning messages:
1: In sam(model, data = Data2, sam.method = "local", ordered = c("x1",  :
  lavaan WARNING: sam() does not support conditional.x = TRUE (yet)
  -> switching to conditional.x = FALSE

Nothing to worry about.  The lavaan() default is to set it TRUE for categorical models, because estimation is more efficient.  It is not a necessity, but the message just let's you know the usual default was changed (for now) in order to use SAM.

2: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

Probably nothing to worry about.  Sometimes solve() fails, so lavaan() tries MASS::ginv() instead.
